content:
maya: heads up — bringing up q4-llama-70b-int8 on the rerank/embedding pipeline and saw a ~6pt NDCG drop on the MTEB-retrieval suite :thinking:

sam: which runner binary/tag? any config diffs vs the float baseline?

maya: rerank-runner v2.3.1 (docker sha: a1b2c3d) on dedicated eval infra. artifacts: float baseline (model:v1.2.0) vs quant int8 (model:q4-int8:v1). embeddings are L2-normalized after quantized forward. CI job: https://ci.internal/redwood/2456

raj: can you paste the raw metric diffs? approximate is fine.

maya: sure — quick paste from eval harness:
```
MTEB retrieval (NDCG@10):
  baseline_float: 0.712
  q4_int8:        0.652
  delta:         -0.060
MRR@10:
  baseline: 0.683
  q4_int8: 0.625
  delta:   -0.058
```

tomas: interesting. my first guess is increased effective sparsity — quant rounding zeroes small dims and hurts fine-grained ranking. also check per-dim scale vs per-channel quantization. seen similar in a previous 8-bit run. :bug:

maya: ran quick stats on embedding norms + per-dim zero-rate:
```
sample_n=5000
mean_norm_float=1.02
mean_norm_q=0.98
per-dim_zero_rate_q (sample): [0.02,0.05,0.11,0.34,0.01,0.00,0.09,...]
mean_zero_rate=0.093
```

eva: that 11-34% on some dims is alarming. could also be index-build sensitivity (HNSW M & efConstruction) — if quant changes magnitude distribution, recall suffers. what index params did runner use?

maya: we use default index config for this eval: M=32, efConstruction=200, efSearch=100. didn't change between runs.

sam: quick sanity check — compute cosine similarity float vs quant per-query for 1k sample queries. run script: 
```bash
python -c "# compute per-query cosine between embeddings from float and quant models"
```
maya: ran it, results:
```
mean_cosine=0.86
median_cosine=0.89
frac_cosine_below_0.6=0.12
topk_overlap@10_mean=0.78
```

raj: topk overlap 78% aligns with ndcg hit. If 12% of queries have cosine <0.6 that's suspicious. Could be class of queries with long tails. Any signal by dataset?

maya: the worst hits are on QA-style queries and short queries (token len <6).

tomas: two action items: 1) measure per-dim quant scale & try per-channel quantization, 2) try small gaussian dither before quant to avoid zeros (stochastic rounding-ish), 3) add guard in CI for big eval regressions. I'll prototype (1) first.

sam: +1. Also add a smoke test in runner CI: compute topk_overlap on a small fixed seed dataset and fail if drop > 10%. Prevents silent regressions.

maya: created draft PR 2345 — fallback path: if avg_cosine < 0.9 then route embedding requests to float path for the smoke dataset and emit alert. Running full eval now.

ci-bot: build/2345 started — unit tests passed, integration eval queued (job id: eval-1851234567-2).

maya: quick update after the patch run — NDCG delta reduced to -0.008 (0.8 pt drop). topk_overlap@10_mean now 0.91. So fallback helps but we need a general fix.

eva: good interim win. we should also add a grafana panel comparing per-dim zero-rate + mean_cosine over time; that would catch future quant model bring-ups. I'll make a dashboard ticket.

sam: long term: upstream quant team should try per-channel scales or 4-bit-aware calibration for embed head. Tomas can you try per-channel quant today?

tomas: on it. I have a quick branch to switch to per-channel symmetric scales for the embed layer. will post results by EOD. :shipit: 

maya: thanks all — for transparency added the raw metric dumps and runner logs to the PR. tagging @platform-observability to get the dashboard ticket linked to the rollout policy.

sam: small follow-up — can we add a unit in eval-harness runner that asserts topk overlap >= 0.9 for the small smoke set? if so, include it in CI gating for model onboarding.

maya: yep i'll add that test in the PR.

raj: nice triage thread. if per-channel fixes still leave corner cases, consider an adaptive hybrid: quant for most traffic, fallback to float for high-risk short queries detected by a simple classifier.

maya: noted. will iterate after Tomas' per-channel run. thanks everyone. :+1:
